issues.detail: Covers mostly happy paths and gotchas but gives no handling for init failure when WebGL/WebGPU is unavailable, asset load errors, context loss, or window resize and cleanup beyond brief notes.
The two examples are prose descriptions of an approach with no runnable code, and the 100,000-particle performance claim is asserted without any measurement or code to support it.

scenarios.name: spritesheet-walk-attack-switch
scenarios.rationale: Both load the sheet with Assets.load, build the AnimatedSprite from the walk animation, set animationSpeed, add it to app.stage and set loop=false for the attack, but A matches the rubric's flow more closely: it sets textures to the attack animation on Space, plays it, and restores the walk textures in onComplete. B also swaps textures and restores walk in onComplete, but it routes everything through a helper and only calls play() through gotoAndPlay(0), so it follows the rubric slightly less literally. B adds a useful JSON-format note, but A's explanations are also accurate.

scenarios.name: speed-up-20k-sprite-snow
scenarios.rationale: Both use Particle with addParticle in one ParticleContainer and position-only dynamicProperties, with no addChild on particles. A updates y with ticker.deltaTime as the rubric asks and wraps at the bottom. B uses ticker.deltaMS/1000 instead, and also updates x every frame with sine sway, so it departs from the rubric's y-only update and deltaTime. B's extra detail (boundsArea, gotchas) is useful but doesn't make up for that.

scenarios.name: v8-init-and-styled-score-hud
scenarios.rationale: A matches more of the rubric: it uses new Application() then await app.init() before app.canvas, loads the font via Assets.load with data: { family }, uses a FillGradient object, draws the bar with rect().fill(), and recommends BitmapText. B recommends BitmapText and uses FillGradient and rect().fill(), but it loads the font with document.fonts.load instead of Assets.load, leaves a junk placeholder block in the code, and scales the bar instead of redrawing it.
